newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Elderly cower without bread in Albanian asylum.
newsitem.headline: Elderly cower without bread in Albanian asylum.

text.p: Residents of an old people's home in the southern Albanian town of Gjirokaster cowered on Thursday in hallways and under staircases, some weeping, as gunfire and explosions erupted in the vicinity.
"We are hiding here under the stairs so we don't get shot," said 59-year old Donika Dauti.
"The situation is getting worse and worse. We're all too old to bear this shock. We should be sitting outside in the sun but it's too dangerous."

Small arms and machine-gun fire broke out around the football stadium in Gjirokaster early on Thursday afternoon in an exchange which included at least one rocket-propelled grenade. The home is about 100 metres (yards) from the stadium.

Gjirokaster, the former administrative centre for southeastern Albania, is now a rebel stronghold. Like most of the south, the town is lawless with armed men roaming the streets night and day firing into the air -- and occasionally at each other.
Residents of the old people's home are paying a physical and psychological price.
Gunmen recently robbed the home's storehouse of a month's supply of food and the 50 residents must now subsist on donations from local businessmen.
"Nobody gets second helpings and the number of calories each of our residents is consuming daily has dropped very sharply," explained the home's director, Jorgo Rapi.
"We have been visited by a number of journalists and even by the Red Cross. The Red Cross said they had food for us but that delivering it was a problem."
Seventy-year old Ilia Culli, blind since boyhood, was in fine if cantankerous form on Thursday on account of the nearby firefight, which lasted about 20 minutes.
"There's something wrong with the electricity today and the bakery isn't working. It's is two o'clock in the afternoon and I haven't had my bread yet today. I really miss it," he said.

"There are two gangs in this town. One pretends to be against the President and uses that as an excuse to start shooting. The other gang is just people who are rubbish and they use the confusion to steal, like they did from us."

The home's director, who gave his name as Mr Rapi, said he was hopeful the situation might improve because a group of masked vigilantes from the nearby town of Tepelene had arrived in Gjirokaster on Wednesday and imposed a night curfew.
"They came last night in masks and armoured cars and they broadcast over megaphones telling everyone to stay inside after eight o'clock or be shot," he explained.
"There was still shooting last night but perhaps it was not as bad as before. I'm hoping they will come back tonight."
Town sources reported that three men had been killed in Gjirokaster on Wednesday evening after two gangs showed up to rob the same place and started firing at one another.
A Swedish journalist was slightly injured in Gjirokaster on Wednesday when he chanced upon a daylight bank robbery in progress and was hit by a stone in the face.
